title: Air-gapped offline bundle import + signature verification flow (Private installer)
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Problem
Air-gapped/on-prem Private customers cannot fetch images/charts/binaries from Redwood registries during upgrades. We need a deterministic offline bundle format and an installer workflow to import + verify that bundle before it can be used for install/upgrade/rollback.

Scope
- Implement offline bundle import command in redwood-private-installer.
- Define bundle structure + manifest format (including digests) and signature validation behavior.
- Ensure verification is mandatory for on-prem/air-gapped mode and failure is safe (no partial state applied).

Non-goals
- Designing a general artifact repository for customers.
- Implementing customer-side signing flows (we will document expected trust root + verification config only).

References
- Confluence: Offline upgrade bundle format (eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/offline-upgrade-bundle-format)
- Confluence: Private release artifact signing & verification standard (eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/private-release-artifact-signing-and-verification)
- Initiative: ENG-2314 (overall upgrade/rollback)
- Security review: ENG-2324

Proposed CLI UX
1) Import
  redwood-private-installer bundle import --file /path/redwood-private-bundle-<id>.tar.zst --store /var/lib/redwood/bundles

2) List
  redwood-private-installer bundle list

3) Show details
  redwood-private-installer bundle inspect <bundle-id>

4) Use during upgrade (follow-on ticket wires this through)
  redwood-private-installer upgrade --bundle <bundle-id>

Bundle format (on disk)
- Delivered as a single file: redwood-private-bundle-<bundle_id>.tar.zst
- After import, expanded into:
  /var/lib/redwood/bundles/<bundle_id>/
    manifest.json
    manifest.sig
    artifacts/
      charts/<chart>.tgz
      images/<image>.tar
      binaries/<installer|tools>
      sbom/<...>

Manifest schema (v1)
Note: stored as JSON. Canonicalization rules for signing: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) so signature is stable across tooling.

Example (illustrative):
{
  "schemaVersion": "1.0",
  "bundleId": "private-2025.03.0+build.2193",
  "createdAt": "2025-02-18T23:51:12Z",
  "release": "private-2025.03",
  "components": {
    "installer": "0.38.0",
    "helmCharts": "2025.03.0",
    "controlPlane": "2.14.1",
    "runtime": "1.21.0"
  },
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "name": "redwood-helm-charts",
      "type": "helm-chart-bundle",
      "path": "artifacts/charts/redwood-private-2025.03.0.tgz",
      "sha256": "<hex>",
      "sizeBytes": 18273491
    },
    {
      "name": "gateway-image",
      "type": "oci-image-tar",
      "path": "artifacts/images/gateway_2.14.1.tar",
      "sha256": "<hex>",
      "sizeBytes": 1643345521
    }
  ],
  "provenance": {
    "buildSystem": "github-actions",
    "sourceRepo": "github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-private-installer",
    "sourceRevision": "<git-sha>",
    "buildId": "<ci-run-id>"
  },
  "signing": {
    "algorithm": "ed25519",
    "keyId": "redwood-release-prod-2025q1",
    "signatureFile": "manifest.sig"
  }
}

Signature verification behavior
- The installer MUST verify the signature over manifest.json (canonicalized with JCS) using a trusted public key set.
- Trusted keys are configured via:
  - /etc/redwood/trust/offline-bundle-keys.d/*.pub (default search path)
  - optional --trust-key /path/to/key.pub (can be specified multiple times)
- keyId in manifest must match one of the trusted keys, unless --allow-unknown-key-id is set (this flag should be hidden/unsafe; intended only for internal debugging).
- No network calls during verification. (Important for true air-gapped environments.)

Integrity verification behavior
- After signature verification, the installer MUST validate that every artifact referenced in the manifest exists and matches sha256 and sizeBytes.
- Validation is streaming (no full file load into memory) to support multi-GB image tarballs.

Failure handling & safety invariants
- Import is atomic:
  - unpack to a temp directory
  - verify signature + digests
  - only then move into the bundle store under its bundleId
- If verification fails:
  - exit non-zero
  - do not persist bundle to store
  - emit a single, operator-actionable error message + error code
- If manifest passes but one artifact digest fails:
  - treat as tampering/corruption; same behavior (no partial import)

Error UX requirements (operator + Support)
- All failures must print:
  - a short summary
  - which check failed (signature vs digest vs missing file)
  - bundleId (if parseable)
  - remediation hints (e.g., "bundle appears corrupted; re-transfer via checksum-verified copy" or "trusted key set does not include keyId=...")
- Also write a structured log line with fields:
  - event=bundle_import_failed
  - reason=<enum>
  - key_id=<string>
  - bundle_path=<string>
  - correlation_id=<uuid>

Audit logging
- For offline import, record an installer-side audit record in the local installer logs (JSON). Follow-up task: when control plane is reachable, forward an audit event (ties into control plane upgrade/rollback audit events).

Telemetry
- Emit metrics:
  - bundle_import_attempt_total{result=success|failure, reason=...}
  - bundle_import_duration_seconds

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `bundle import` command supports .tar.zst input and imports into bundle store with atomic behavior.
- [ ] Mandatory signature verification of manifest using trusted key(s); no network dependency.
- [ ] Full artifact integrity verification using sha256 + size before bundle is accepted.
- [ ] Clear, documented error modes and exit codes for: invalid signature, unknown keyId, missing artifact, digest mismatch, unsupported schemaVersion.
- [ ] Unit tests for parser/canonicalization + signature validation.
- [ ] Integration tests for corrupted bundle and wrong-key bundle.
- [ ] Docs snippet added to customer-facing Private upgrade docs (handoff to Docs ticket) describing required steps and common errors.

Implementation notes
- Use libsodium/ed25519 verification (matches the Release Eng standard). Avoid PGP to keep verification implementation small and deterministic.
- Canonicalization: adopt an existing JCS library (Go) rather than rolling our own. Ensure we lock a version.
- Ensure we do not log full paths to sensitive directories by default (only the bundle file path the operator passed).

Open questions
- Key rotation / multiple valid keys: installer supports multiple keys now. Need Security sign-off on how key IDs map to public keys and what the default trust store should include for GA.
- Should we allow a mode where the manifest is signed but per-artifact digests are optional? Current position: NO (digests required) to protect transfer corruption/tampering.

Risks
- Large image bundles may make import time exceed maintenance window. Mitigation: make import a separate pre-step that can be done earlier; import only validates + stores, does not apply changes.

Owner(s)
- Devon Price (implementation)
- Hanae Suzuki + Marcus Lin (signing trust model review)
- Connor O’Brien (release integration)

Links
- Confluence: offline-upgrade-bundle-format
- Confluence: private-release-artifact-signing-and-verification
comments: 2025-01-16 — Connor O'Brien: Creating this as the concrete implementation behind the bundle format doc. Please keep CLI + error codes aligned with what Support will copy/paste into runbooks.

2025-01-23 — Devon Price: Drafted `bundle import` skeleton and temp-dir unpack. Next: wire in signature verification + JCS canonicalization. Question: do we want to allow `--trust-key` multiple times (I think yes for rotation)?

2025-01-24 — Marcus Lin: Yes, multiple trust keys is required for rotation. Also, no network calls. Make sure we fail closed if keyId is unknown (no "best effort" verification). Please route any debug bypass behind an internal-only flag and default it off.

2025-01-28 — Hanae Suzuki: For key storage, propose `/etc/redwood/trust/offline-bundle-keys.d/*.pub` owned by root, 0644. Document how customers install/update keys. KeyId should be embedded in filename too, e.g. `redwood-release-prod-2025q1.pub`.

2025-02-03 — Devon Price: Implemented signature verification (ed25519) and digest checks streaming SHA256. Added exit codes: 21 invalid_signature, 22 unknown_key, 23 digest_mismatch, 24 missing_artifact, 25 unsupported_schema. Working on better remediation hints + structured logs.

2025-02-11 — Sean Gallagher: Please ensure import is atomic and leaves no partial dirs under `/var/lib/redwood/bundles`. We hit a similar issue in a prior on-prem installer where a failed unpack filled the disk. Clean up temp on failure and add a disk-space precheck as a follow-up.

2025-02-18 — Devon Price: Added atomic move into bundle store and temp cleanup; integration tests cover corrupted sig + corrupted artifact tar. Ready for Security review of trust store defaults + bypass flag.

2025-02-21 — Dr. Aisha Rahman: Security review note: confirm JCS canonicalization library is pinned and verified; add test vectors to prevent canonicalization drift. Also ensure logs do not print public key material or raw signature bytes.
